# Widgets

A widget type is declared once in the manifest and bound once in code. The
declaration is DURABLE: the canvas stores documents against it, so its type name,
prop names and group names outlive any particular implementation.

## Declaring

| field | type | required | rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | string | yes | at most 128 characters |
| `title` | string | yes | at least 1 character; at most 80 characters |
| `description` | string | no | at most 500 characters |
| `icon` | string | no | asset paths are ./-relative POSIX, no .., no schemes |
| `category` | `Cards` \| `3D` \| `Nodes` \| `Tools` | no | — |
| `preview` | one of `color`, `gradient`, `asset` | no | discriminated by `kind` |
| `schemaVersion` | number | yes | `integer; > 0` |
| `surface` | `dom` \| `gl` | yes | — |
| `sizeMode` | `fixed` \| `auto-height` \| `auto` | yes | — |
| `defaultSize` | { w: number, h: number } | yes | — |
| `minSize` | { w: number, h: number } | no | — |
| `maxSize` | { w: number, h: number } | no | — |
| `interaction` | { selectable?: boolean, movable?: boolean, resizable?: boolean, snap?: `source` \| `target` \| `both` \| `none`, dragOn?: `press` \| `longPress`, solid?: boolean, sweepContained?: boolean, keyboard?: `shared` \| `exclusive`, keyboardEscape?: `release` \| `widget` } | no | — |
| `container` | `{ accepts: string[], provides?: string[] }` | no | — |
| `provides` | `string[]` | no | at most 16 item(s) |
| `ports` | { id: string, side: `n` \| `e` \| `s` \| `w`, index?: number, accepts?: string[] }[] | no | at most 16 item(s) |
| `props` | object mapping name → one of `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum`, `json`, `entity-ref`, `session-ref`, `terminal-ref`, `artifact-ref`, `file-ref` | no | discriminated by `kind`; defaults to `{}` |
| `groups` | `object mapping name → string[]` | no | at least 1 item(s); defaults to `{}` |

`surface` picks the renderer: `dom` for an HTML card, `gl` for a 3D island with
DOM chrome portaled under it. `sizeMode` and `defaultSize` set the prefab the
host builds; `interaction` carries the canvas's own flags (selectable, movable,
resizable, snap, dragOn, solid, sweepContained).

## Props

Props are the widget's durable data. Each is one of these kinds:

| kind | fields | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `optional`, `mutable`, `default`, `maxLength` | — |
| `number` | `optional`, `mutable`, `default`, `min`, `max` | — |
| `boolean` | `optional`, `mutable`, `default` | — |
| `enum` | `optional`, `mutable`, `options`, `default` | — |
| `json` | `optional`, `mutable`, `inner`, `default`, `maxBytes` | `inner` describes the nested shape; the value rides one string cell |
| `entity-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `session-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `terminal-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `artifact-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `file-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |

Every kind also accepts `optional` and `mutable` (default true). A default must
satisfy its own spec — an enum default outside `options`, a number outside
`min`/`max`, a string over `maxLength` are all refused at emit.

## Conflict groups

Props that change together belong in a named group. The name is durable: the
engine generates a component named `<widget type>:<group name>` from it, and two
editors writing different groups of the same widget never conflict.

- Omitting `groups` is the common case — ungrouped props join the engine's
  default `props` group.
- A group name matches `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, every member must be a declared prop,
  and a prop belongs to at most one group.
- An immutable prop (`mutable: false`) belongs to no group at all.

```ts
props: {
  title: { kind: "string", default: "" },
  body: { kind: "string", default: "" },
  color: { kind: "enum", options: ["amber", "slate"], default: "amber" },
},
groups: {
  text: ["title", "body"],   // one editor typing
  style: ["color"],          // another recolouring — no conflict
},
```

## Ports

A node-style widget declares ports; the engine renders and routes the wires.
Each port has an `id`, a `side` (`n`/`e`/`s`/`w`), an optional `index` along that
side, and an optional `accepts` list. Omitting `accepts` means it connects to
anything. Port ids are unique within a widget.

## Binding

One `register` per declared type, during `activate`:

```ts
ctx.widgets.register({
  type: "com.example.notes",
  binding: {
    component: NoteCard,      // the card itself
    chrome: NoteChrome,       // GL only: DOM chrome under the canvas
    animated: true,           // GL only: per-frame island repaint
    preview: NotePreview,     // tray preview override
  },
});
```

`register` throws on an undeclared type and on a second bind of the same type in
one activation. It returns a `Disposable`; the host disposes the binding when
the activation ends, so you do not have to.

## Reading and writing props

The canvas hooks arrive through the SDK's `/canvas` door, never from ICE
directly:

```tsx
import { useOps, useWidgetProps, type WidgetComponentProps } from "@vibefield/plugin-sdk/canvas";

const TYPE = "com.example.notes";

function NoteCard({ world, entity }: WidgetComponentProps) {
  const props = useWidgetProps<{ body: string }>(world, entity, TYPE);
  const ops = useOps();
  return (
    <textarea
      value={props.body}
      onChange={(e) => ops.setWidgetProps(entity, { body: e.target.value })}
    />
  );
}
```
